properties.title: Central American Vegetation/Land Cover Classification and Conservation Status
properties.description: The Central American Vegetation/Land Cover Classification and Conservation Status consists of GIS coverages of vegetation classes (forests, woodlands, savannas, shrubs, grasslands, wetlands, rocks, sand, soils, inland waters, parks and reserves) for Central America, derived from 1-kilometer resolution Advanced Very High Resolution Radiometer (AVHRR) imagery. This data set is produced by Proyecto Ambiental Regional de Centroamerica/Central America Protected Areas Systems (PROARCA/CAPAS), a conservation partnership of the Central American Commission on Environment and Development (CCAD), U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID), International Resources Group, Ltd. (IRG), The Nature Conservancy (TNC), Winrock International (WI), and is distributed by the Columbia University Center for International Earth Science Information Network (CIESIN).
keywords: EARTH SCIENCE > HUMAN DIMENSIONS > ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS > CONSERVATION
EARTH SCIENCE > LAND SURFACE > SURFACE THERMAL PROPERTIES > LAND SURFACE TEMPERATURE
properties.ciesin:tags: Country, Biota, Farming, Geoscientific Information, Imagery/Base Maps/Earth Cover, Inland Waters, Oceans, Conservation, Land Use, Remote Sensing, Earth Science, Land Surface, Surface Thermal Properties, Land Surface Temperature, Human Dimensions, Environmental Impacts
properties.ciesin:purpose: To identify remaining natural vegetation types in Central America.
properties.ciesin:supplemental_info: The data set used in this gap analysis is comprised of the most spatially detailed data set on protected areas, vegetation, and ecoregion data ever assembled for the region as a whole. The following digital geospatial data were compiled for the gap analysis: Country boundaries (Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Panama, 1:1 Million, Digital Chart of the World, ESRI, Inc. 1993); Vegetation and Landcover map (1:2 Million, PROARCA/CAPAS, 1998); Mesoamerican protected areas network systems (1:1 Million, WCS, 1996); Digital Elevation Model (1 km grid, USGS EROS Data Center, 1996); Ecoregions (1:15 Million, Dinerstein, et al., 1995).
